as_told.title: Göbekli Tepe pushing back the age of civilization

plain: Göbekli Tepe, an ancient stone site in Turkey, is said by some to be the place where civilisation began, earlier than Egypt. The podcaster Joe Rogan says on the show that "a lot of people think" Turkey, not Egypt, "might have been the origin of civilization," and points to the site. Michels comes back to it again and again in his own words. In one episode he calls it an ancient burial site "dating as far back as 9000 BC" and built from "50 ton blocks." In another he dates it to about 11,000 years ago, credits the writer Graham Hancock's book Fingerprints of the Gods and National Geographic, and says it "rewrites the map" of how old human civilisation is. Rogan only calls it a possible origin, but Michels goes further. In a third episode he says every 30 or 40 years a new find pushes the date back, and Göbekli Tepe may not even be the earliest site built from giant stones. If they are right, complex human society is much older than the usual story allows.
